status_language: protection_identified -> part_selected; coordination NOT demonstrated; hardware NOT verified

one_circuit.summary: ONE arrangement: a series high-speed DC-rated fuse in the DC bus (in the internal discharge loop), the existing line-to-neutral MOV for the surge case, and the existing line fuse for the line-fed case.

new_part.placement: in series in the DC bus between the boost-diode (U10) cathode and the capacitor bank (on the PFC_BUS_PLUS_390V conductor)
new_part.why_here: this conductor is common to the internal discharge loop (caps -> shorted U10 -> U9 -> caps); a series element on it carries the entire discharge and opens the loop irrespective of U9 health
new_part.rating_source: Cooper Bussmann High Speed Fuses catalogue page, Data Sheet 720025 (FWP 690V/700V, 1-50 A), 14x51 mm ferrule, FWP-50A14F row
new_part.rating_source_condition: clearing I2t published at rated voltage and power factor 0.15 (AC/inductive test); NOT a 400 Vdc capacitor-discharge condition

existing_mov.manufacturer_vi_figure: LA Series Transient V-I Characteristics, Maximum Clamping Voltage for 14mm Parts, Figure 10, page 7, Rev VL 16/9/2024

existing_line_fuse.role: only series interrupting element in the line-fed loop

fault_cases.name: U10 shorted, U9 healthy
fault_cases.loop: caps -> shorted U10 -> a1 -> U9 -> caps (internal)
fault_cases.candidate_interrupter: F2 (FWP-50A14F) by I2t; alternatively U9 commanded off
fault_cases.why: F2 is topologically in the loop and melts when the pulse action E/R exceeds 200 A2s (R_loop < 0.896 ohm, illustrative). U9 can open the path in principle, but no loop-current detection exists (the shunt U12 is not in the loop and the controller has no OCP), so the detection/latency budget is unquantified and turn-off is not credited.
fault_cases.detection_latency_budget_required: a dedicated loop-current sense (e.g. a current transformer or an in-loop shunt) plus a gate driver with desaturation, tripping within the U9 short-circuit SOA; no such path exists on the board

fault_cases.name: U10 shorted, U9 failed short
fault_cases.loop: caps -> shorted U10 -> a1 -> shorted U9 -> caps (internal)
fault_cases.why: U9 cannot be turned off; no gate command opens a failed-short switch. Only the series fuse F2 can act. Whether F2 clears is NOT demonstrated: the prospective peak and action I2t depend on an unestablished loop resistance, and the published clearing I2t is an AC/inductive figure, not a 400 Vdc capacitor-discharge figure. If demonstrated clearing is required, NO available part interrupts case (b).

fault_cases.name: line-fed switch short with the bridge following
fault_cases.loop: mains -> F1 -> CMC -> NTC/bypass -> bridge -> U8 -> shorted U9 -> U12 -> bridge return
fault_cases.why: F1 is the only series element by topology, but its breaking capacity is 160 A at 250 VAC and the prospective line current is unestablished; coordination with the surviving bridge/switch SOA is NOT demonstrated. F2 is not in this loop.

fault_cases.name: line surge
fault_cases.candidate_element: U7 (V150LA10AP MOV) - clamps, does not interrupt
fault_cases.why: The MOV diverts the surge; the required clamp at the operating surge current is not resolvable because that current is not established (the datasheet 395 V max is an upper bound at 50 A only). The surge contract (IEC 61000-4-5, 1 kV L-L / 2 kV L-PE) is PROVISIONAL/ASSUMED.

fault_cases.name: faults the arrangement cannot interrupt
items: internal capacitor discharge if F2 does not clear (clearing not demonstrated)
any already-bolted short: no gate command opens a failed-short device
a crowbar alone (diverts, does not interrupt; not part of this arrangement)
a line-fed fault below F1's clearing threshold
line-to-PE / common-mode surge (the MOV is line-to-neutral only)
case (b) if demonstrated clearing is required
